intrebari.intrebare: Which saint's day, Scotland's national day, is celebrated on 30 November?
intrebari.explicatie: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland. St David is Welsh, St Patrick Irish, St George English.

intrebari.intrebare: Scotland's flag, the Saltire, shows St Andrew's cross. What does it look like?
variante: a white diagonal cross on a blue background
a red cross on a white background
a red diagonal cross on a white background
a yellow cross on a black background
intrebari.explicatie: According to tradition, St Andrew was crucified on an X-shaped cross.

intrebari.intrebare: Since 2007, St Andrew's Day has officially been a ______ in Scotland.
intrebari.explicatie: The St Andrew's Day Bank Holiday (Scotland) Act was passed in 2007.

intrebari.intrebare: Which Scottish dish, made from sheep's offal, oatmeal and spices, is often served at St Andrew's Day celebrations?
intrebari.explicatie: Haggis is Scotland's best-known national dish.

intrebari.intrebare: Complete the traditional rhyme: 'Remember, remember, the fifth of November, gunpowder, treason and ______.'
intrebari.explicatie: The rhyme recalls the Gunpowder Plot of 1605.

intrebari.intrebare: What is traditionally burned on top of bonfires on 5 November?
variante: a 'guy' — a figure of Guy Fawkes
intrebari.explicatie: The effigy is called a 'guy', after Guy Fawkes.

intrebari.intrebare: What did children traditionally ask passers-by for in the days before Bonfire Night?
intrebari.explicatie: Children showed the guy they had made and collected money for fireworks.

intrebari.intrebare: Bonfires were first lit in London in November 1605 to celebrate...
intrebari.explicatie: Londoners lit bonfires to celebrate that James I had survived the plot.

intrebari.intrebare: The informal English word 'guy' (meaning 'man') comes from...
intrebari.explicatie: First it meant a strangely dressed person (like the effigy), then simply 'a man'.

intrebari.intrebare: In parts of northern England, 4 November — the night before Bonfire Night — is traditionally known as...
intrebari.explicatie: On Mischief Night, children traditionally played harmless pranks.

intrebari.intrebare: Which sticky ginger cake made with oatmeal and treacle is traditionally eaten on Bonfire Night, especially in Yorkshire?
intrebari.explicatie: Parkin is often baked days in advance because it gets stickier with time.

intrebari.intrebare: Bonfire toffee, eaten on 5 November in northern England, is made mainly with...
intrebari.explicatie: Its dark colour and strong taste come from black treacle.

intrebari.intrebare: Which town in East Sussex is famous for its huge Bonfire Night processions organised by local bonfire societies?
intrebari.explicatie: Lewes holds the largest Bonfire Night celebrations in the UK.

intrebari.intrebare: In Ottery St Mary, Devon, people celebrate 5 November by running through the streets carrying...
intrebari.explicatie: The Tar Barrels tradition is centuries old.

intrebari.intrebare: Because of the Gunpowder Plot, before every State Opening of Parliament the cellars of the Palace of Westminster are ceremonially searched by...
intrebari.explicatie: The ceremonial search has taken place for centuries.

intrebari.intrebare: Which Christian festival is celebrated on 1 November?
intrebari.explicatie: All Saints' Day is 1 November; All Souls' Day follows on 2 November.

intrebari.intrebare: In the old farming calendar, 11 November is the feast of St Martin, also known as...
intrebari.explicatie: Martinmas was a traditional time for hiring fairs and preparing food for winter.

intrebari.intrebare: What is the main symbol of Remembrance in the UK each November?
intrebari.explicatie: Poppies grew on the battlefields of Flanders in the First World War.

intrebari.intrebare: The poppy became a symbol of remembrance partly thanks to the poem 'In Flanders Fields', written in 1915 by...
intrebari.explicatie: John McCrae was a Canadian army doctor.

intrebari.intrebare: Which charity runs the annual Poppy Appeal in the UK?
intrebari.explicatie: The money raised supports members of the armed forces, veterans and their families.

intrebari.intrebare: How is the Scottish remembrance poppy different from the one sold in England?
variante: it has four petals and no leaf
it has a thistle in the centre
intrebari.explicatie: The English poppy has two petals and a green leaf.

intrebari.intrebare: Some people wear a white poppy in November. What does it represent?
variante: peace, and remembering all victims of war
intrebari.explicatie: The purple poppy is the one that remembers animals.

intrebari.intrebare: Remembrance Sunday is held on...
intrebari.explicatie: Armistice Day is always 11 November; Remembrance Sunday is the second Sunday of the month.

intrebari.intrebare: Where does the national Remembrance Sunday ceremony take place?
intrebari.explicatie: The ceremony is broadcast live on national television.

intrebari.intrebare: Who traditionally lays the first wreath at the Cenotaph on Remembrance Sunday?
intrebari.explicatie: The monarch lays the first wreath, followed by other members of the royal family and political leaders.

intrebari.intrebare: Which bugle call is played at Remembrance ceremonies just before the two-minute silence?
intrebari.explicatie: The Last Post is followed by the silence and then by Reveille.

intrebari.intrebare: The lines 'They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old' are read at Remembrance services. Who wrote them?
intrebari.explicatie: They come from Binyon's poem 'For the Fallen' (1914).

intrebari.intrebare: The Royal British Legion's Festival of Remembrance is held each November at which London venue?
intrebari.explicatie: It takes place on the Saturday before Remembrance Sunday.

intrebari.intrebare: The Armistice took effect at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the ______ month.
intrebari.explicatie: November is the eleventh month of the year.

intrebari.intrebare: Which British TV series was first broadcast on 23 November 1963?
intrebari.explicatie: Doctor Who is one of the longest-running science fiction series in the world.

intrebari.intrebare: In Doctor Who, the Doctor's time machine, the TARDIS, looks like a...
intrebari.explicatie: TARDIS stands for 'Time And Relative Dimension In Space'.

intrebari.intrebare: Which actor played the first Doctor in Doctor Who, starting in November 1963?
intrebari.explicatie: Hartnell played the role from 1963 to 1966.

intrebari.intrebare: Which Agatha Christie play opened in London's West End on 25 November 1952 and became the world's longest-running play?
intrebari.explicatie: Apart from a break during the COVID-19 pandemic, it has run continuously since 1952.

intrebari.intrebare: What is the name of the yellow bear with a spotty bandage over one eye who is the mascot of the BBC's Children in Need appeal?
intrebari.explicatie: Children in Need holds its big fundraising TV evening every November.

intrebari.intrebare: During 'Movember', many men raise money for men's health by...
intrebari.explicatie: The name combines 'moustache' and 'November'.

intrebari.intrebare: Which English city is famous for one of the biggest Diwali celebrations outside India?
intrebari.explicatie: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, usually falls in October or November.

intrebari.intrebare: Stir-up Sunday, the last Sunday before Advent (usually in late November), is the traditional day for making...
intrebari.explicatie: Family members take turns stirring the mixture and making a wish.

intrebari.intrebare: Which annual procession takes place in the City of London in November, when the new Lord Mayor travels in a golden coach?
intrebari.explicatie: The Lord Mayor's Show dates back more than 800 years.

intrebari.intrebare: In many UK towns and cities, November is the month when crowds gather for the...
intrebari.explicatie: Famous celebrities are often invited to switch on the lights.

intrebari.intrebare: Bonfire Night is also widely known as...
intrebari.explicatie: Burns Night (25 January) celebrates the poet Robert Burns.
